course_description:
This course aims to provide final year students with the opportunity to apply conceptual knowledge to the real world via a professional placement. As such, this course strongly links discipline learnings, personal employability skills and attributes developed by students across the duration of their studies with the challenges and expectations of working in industry. In doing so, students have the opportunity to gain valuable work experience in their chosen profession and to connect this experience to the development of a workplace ready skill-set. Successful completion of the course will provide students with the employability skills required for transition to the world of work. Further information about how to apply for RBUS3999 can be found on the BEL Faculty's work-integrated learning website .

Placement/Internship requirements

Prior to enrolling in this course, you should independently secure a work placement that's relevant to your field of study. The organisation should be willing to host you, provide meaningful work that supports the development of your skills and capabilities, and appoint an experienced industry supervisor to oversee your work, provide guidance, and offer feedback on your performance. Support is available from the BEL Faculty Employability Team to help you source an appropriate host organisation.

Your industry placement (internship) should comprise between 80 and 100 hours of professional work experience, throughout (or before) the semester.ﾠAs an example, you might choose to complete your internship in one block of 3 or 4 weeks full-time,ﾠ3 days a week over 4-5 weeks, orﾠ2 days a week over 7-8 weeks.ﾠCompleting one day a week of your internship hours is notﾠrecommended as experience has shown the likelihood of you being given realistic work tasks and/or being included in the work team is significantly reduced. If completing your internship at your current employer, you must undertake higher level duties that are different from your usual role for 80-100 hours.

Domestic internships that are unpaid must be approved. All international internships must be paid

After securing your internship you need to apply for approval before you will be allowed to enrol on this course. You must complete the WIL application process, including submission of a Learning Agreement and Internship Information Form.

The course is offered four times a year to make alignment with your internship dates possible. Your internship should be as close as possible to the course start date.

If your internship commencement date is too far removed from the course start date, you may be advised to source a new internship.

NOTE: Before you commence your internship, it is important you first refer to the BEL Work-integrated Learning (WIL) website to familiarise yourself with the process of having your internship approved before it can be considered suitable for course credit. Access the BEL Internships website at my.uq.edu.au .

course_aims: This course gives students the opportunity to link discipline learnings, employability skills and personal attributes with the challenges and expectations of working in industry. It is designed to help students identify their unique strengths and build a strong professional identity. The course will reflectively deepen students’ understanding of workplace practices, processes and challenges. Ultimately, the course will help students emerge with the confidence and skills to thrive in the modern workplace.

assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment, you will showcase your reflective skills by analysing and reflecting on the business/organisation you observed and engaged with during your placement. You will critically reflect on the practices, processes, challenges and/or successes of the business or organisation you worked in. Your observations will lead you to develop a foundational understanding of how businesses operate, their managerial decision-making, and how businesses respond to wider industry/economic forces. The assessment will consist of two parts: A2.1: A written reflection that presents your observations and critical analysis of a significant/consequential practice, process, challenge, and/or opportunity within the business or organisation in which you worked. The reflection should also explore the key learnings gained from this experience and explicitly link these insights to the development of your skills and personal attributes. A2.2: A semi-structured consultation with your lecturer during which you will discuss the issue you identified in A2.1, as well as the learnings you gained with reference to your employability skillset and attributes. assessment_details.title: A3. Professional Development Plan
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment you will write a comprehensive and self-reflective Professional Development Plan. You will evaluate your employability in the context of: self-evaluation of your placement performance, feedback you receive from supervisors/mentors/colleagues, various self-test instruments, research into job/industry requirements and trends, as well as UQ’s graduate attributes. You will identify specific areas for improvement (development areas), and develop a clear action plan to achieve your development goals. The assessment concludes with a strategic perspective of your professional identity and long-term career aspirations. You will consider career pathways that align with your goals for both personal and professional growth. Read full task description Hide full task description
